label: Search Exceeded the Scope of Consent
motion_heading: The Search Exceeded the Scope of Any Consent Given

review_conditions.display_note: You aren't sure yet how police justified the search. This section was drafted anyway; find out from the reports and the prosecution's response what justification they claim before filing, or cut this section.

rule_statements.text: When a search is authorized by consent, its scope is limited by the terms of that authorization.
The scope of consent is measured by what a reasonable person would have understood from the exchange between the officer and the person consenting.
A person may limit the scope of the search to which they consent.
Consent may be withdrawn, and a search that continues after withdrawal is no longer supported by consent.

practice_notes: Pin down the exact words of the request and the answer — 'can I look in your car?' is narrower than 'can I search your car?', and what was said about the object of the search matters.
If your client objected or limited the search partway through, find out whether it's on video.
_author_notes: withdrawal has no authority: I'm not certain of a Supreme Court case holding that consent can be withdrawn mid-search, so it's left as a gap. Ninth Circuit and Alaska authority not researched.
